correctness.rationale: Directly recomputed the 32 distinct codewords from the exact 5x20 integer columns. Exactly thirty nonzero messages have two all-zero cyclic three-windows and the remaining one has none. Every three-consecutive-column system has precisely three nonzero orthogonal messages; summing gives 60. For any rank-five binary generator with minimum three-symbol distance at least n-2, each of its 31 nonzero messages has at most two zero three-windows and each position has at least three nonzero annihilators, so 3n<=62 and n<=20. At n20,d18, the Griesmer equality 7n=ceil(72)+ceil(36)+ceil(18)+ceil(9)+ceil(4.5)=140 matches; Singleton is d3<=n-2.

value.rationale: The natural cutoff problem asks the maximum length of a dimension-five binary three-read Singleton-optimal linear code. The general 2024 Griesmer bound already gives nonexistence beyond length 20, but does not guarantee any realizing example. An explicit rank-five n20 code with all 31 weights computed gives definitive attainability, meeting two independent fundamental bounds and closing that natural gap. No broad theorem or uniqueness claim is asserted. Its exact parameters and simple reproducible certificate can serve as a boundary test case for constructions and geometric packing models.
